x: Southern Area, started the field of 114 walkers, and C. Williams of Ilford A.C., the favourite, was soon in the lead and retained this to finish a very worthy winner from A.G.

Colin Williams (Ilford A.C) won his first A.A.A. title and had the double honour of being awarded the style prize also. Ray Middleton finished a meritorious third behind Williams and Arthur Thomson of Metropolitan.

Jack's effort over 5½ miles at Bexley was against even tougher opposition. In gaining sixth place he was beaten by C.Williams, M.Tolley, P.Selby, J.Moran and J.Godber, with less than 90 seconds covering all six.
Singh scampered thro' the first lap in 94.3 secs. revelling in his moment of glory with Matthews, Vickers, Colin Williams, Adjit Singh and Lindner hard on his heels.

Kelly pushed our jumping reputation a bit higher, by winning the youths' long-jump, and had two good sprint performances to his credit by the end of the evening, as well. Only one of our members figure in the Boys' results, but C. Williams, with two first and a third, kent us to the front of the picture.

Matthews and Vickers were in tow and then came Colin Williams, Adjit Singh and Lindner. But the inevitable happened, Zora had thrown caution to the winds with his effort and after half a mile the judges pulled him out, a fate that soon befell his fellow countryman and two of the Germans.
